chunks: From al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A Jew, a Christian, and a Zoroastrian are not to be made to swear by anything other than Allah, for Allah the Exalted says: 'Judge between them by what Allah has revealed.'

key_terms.احْكُم بَيْنَهُم بِمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ: Judge between them by what Allah has revealed
key_terms.يُحَلَّفُ: to be made to swear an oath

ai.seo_question: Who should non-Muslims be made to swear by in Islamic legal contexts?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records the general principle that non-Muslims are sworn by Allah, while noting the apparent exception of Imam Ali swearing a Jew by the Torah. Shia scholars reconcile this by distinguishing between the Imam's authority to use their specific scriptures for practical efficacy (rad') and the general prohibition for others who lack that knowledge, a nuance further supported by reports affirming that each faith is sworn by what they hold sacred.
